name: FreeShow
shortDescription: Free, open-source display software for songs, Bible passages and media. It can use stage displays and several outputs during a service.
suitableContexts: Churches seeking a free presentation tool
Teams that need multi-output displays and are willing to learn a newer application

pricing.summary: FreeShow states that it is free and open source, with no subscription or trial requirement. Churches should still budget for hardware, training, media assets, backup arrangements and any licensed Bible or song content.

tiers.label: FreeShow
tiers.detail: The supplier describes FreeShow as a free, open-source non-profit project

importExport: Imports from PowerPoint, ProPresenter, EasyWorship and OpenSong

editorial.assessment: FreeShow is a capable no-licence-cost alternative for teams prepared to own their setup, training and live-service resilience. It should be evaluated in a full rehearsal, including displays, lyrics, Bible licensing, media and a fall-back plan, rather than only at a desk.
bestFor: Cost-conscious churches with volunteers who can rehearse and support the system
Teams needing multi-output, remote control or planning-system connections
strengths: Supplier lists multi-output, remote control and several import options
limitations: The project material does not describe a paid supplier-support option
Churches remain responsible for content licences, hardware and live-service contingency

procurementVerdict.problem: Cost-conscious churches with volunteers who can rehearse and support the system
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Decide who will support the software during a live service

longForm.verdict: FreeShow is worth a serious rehearsal for churches that need more than basic slides but do not want recurring presentation-software fees. Its low price does not remove the need for training, tested outputs and a reliable Sunday-morning backup.

decisionLens.heading: A free tool should still pass a live-service resilience test.
decisionLens.text: Run a rehearsal on the actual computer, displays, projector, network and operator hand-off the church uses. Include lyrics, Bible passages, videos, stage display and a recovery from a failed output before changing the live-service setup.

sections.heading: Feature-rich presentation without a licence charge
sections.question: Can the team operate it confidently under live pressure?
paragraphs: FreeShow describes scripture and lyric tools, flexible slide editing, timed play, multiple outputs, NDI support, remote control and cloud sync. It also lists imports from several established presentation packages.

Use a real service plan as the test file, not a small sample. Confirm that the required Bible translations and song lyrics are available under the church’s existing licences, and keep an independent backup for the first live services.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score. It is based on FreeShow’s official product and documentation pages.
themes: No subscription cost can make full rehearsal easier to justify.
The risk moves toward volunteer training, hardware and live-service support.
userFeedback.caveat: Supplier feature claims are not independent testing, and free software does not confer permission to display or stream licensed content.

faq.question: Is FreeShow free?
faq.answer: Yes. FreeShow describes itself as a free, open-source project and says it will remain free.

faq.question: Does FreeShow offer a trial?
faq.answer: No trial is needed because the software is free to download and use.

faq.question: Can FreeShow import existing presentations?
faq.answer: Yes, according to the supplier. It lists imports from PowerPoint, ProPresenter, EasyWorship and OpenSong among others.

faq.question: Does FreeShow include song and Bible licences?
faq.answer: Churches remain responsible for their own Bible, song and streaming licences.
